senses.en: below zero, before a number of degrees: 零下五度 'minus five degrees'
on its own: below freezing (晚上会到零下)

examples.zh: 明天零下五度，多穿一点儿。
examples.en: It'll be minus five tomorrow, so wear an extra layer.
examples.analysis: 零下 + number + 度 gives a temperature below zero: 零下五度 'minus five degrees' (Celsius in China). The temperature itself is the predicate; no 是 is needed. 多穿一点儿 'wear a bit more' is the advice that usually follows.

examples.en: Will it drop below zero tonight?
examples.analysis: Here 零下 stands alone, with no number: 'below zero, below freezing'. 到 'reach' + 零下 = 'get down to below zero'. 会 marks a prediction, and 吗 turns it into a yes-or-no question.

examples.en: In Hanoi, it doesn't go below zero in winter.
examples.analysis: 不会到零下 'won't get down below zero': 不会 rules something out, here as a general fact about the climate rather than one night's forecast. 河内冬天 'Hanoi in winter' sets the scene at the front.

senses.en: volleyball, the sport (the verb is 打: 打排球)
a volleyball, the ball itself

examples.en: Can you play volleyball?
examples.analysis: The verb for volleyball is 打 'hit, play', as in 打篮球 and 打网球. 会 here asks about a learned skill: 'do you know how to play?'. 吗 makes it a yes-or-no question.

examples.zh: 我们周末去海边打排球吧。
examples.en: Let's go play volleyball at the beach this weekend.
examples.analysis: 去 + place + activity: 去海边打排球 'go to the beach to play volleyball'. The place comes right after 去, then what you'll do there. 周末 sits before the verbs as the time, and 吧 turns the plan into a suggestion.

examples.zh: 我不太喜欢排球，我喜欢篮球。
examples.en: I'm not really into volleyball. I like basketball.
examples.analysis: Here 排球 is the sport as something you like or not, the object of 喜欢. 不太喜欢 'don't really like' is softer than a flat 不喜欢. The second clause gives the contrast with no word for 'but'.

senses.en: jiaozi: crescent-shaped filled dumplings, usually boiled (水饺), also steamed (蒸饺) or pan-fried (煎饺)

measure.note: 一个饺子; 一碗饺子 'a bowl of dumplings'

examples.zh: 过年的时候，我们家都吃饺子。
examples.en: At New Year, our family always eats dumplings.
examples.analysis: 吃饺子 'eat dumplings' is the everyday verb-object pair. 都 here covers every New Year: 'each time, without fail'. In northern China, dumplings are the classic New Year's Eve meal.

examples.zh: 你想吃什么？饺子还是面条儿？
examples.en: What do you feel like eating? Dumplings or noodles?
examples.analysis: 饺子还是面条儿 'dumplings or noodles?': 还是 between two options makes a choice question, so no 吗 is used. 饺子 needs no measure word here because it names the dish, not a number of pieces.

examples.en: Did you make these dumplings yourself?
examples.analysis: The verb for making dumplings is 包 'wrap': 包饺子. 饺子 comes first as the topic. 是…的 asks about a detail of a past action, here who did it: 你自己 'you yourself'.

senses.en: a sunny day; clear, fine weather (opposite: 阴天 'overcast day')

examples.zh: 今天是晴天，我们出去走走吧。
examples.en: It's a sunny day today. Let's go out for a walk.
examples.analysis: 晴天 is a noun, so here it comes after 是: 今天是晴天 'today is a sunny day' (casual speech and forecasts often drop 是: 明天晴天). With the adjective 晴, people say 天晴了 'it has cleared up'. 走走 'walk a little' is the relaxed, doubled form of 走.

examples.en: Is it going to be sunny or cloudy tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 是 A 还是 B 'is it A or B?' is a choice question, so no 吗. 晴天 and 阴天 are the standard pair in weather talk: a clear day versus an overcast one.

examples.en: We haven't had a sunny day in ages.
examples.analysis: 好久没有…了 'there hasn't been … for a long time': 没有 + noun says it hasn't been around, and the final 了 shows the situation has lasted up to now. A typical complaint in a rainy spell.

meaning: to walk into; to enter (a room, a building)

senses.en: to walk into a place: 走进 + place (走进教室)

examples.zh: 我走进房间的时候，他正在睡觉。
examples.en: When I walked into the room, he was sleeping.
examples.analysis: 走进 + place: the place goes straight after 走进, with no 到 or 在. 走 is the movement and 进 the direction 'into'. 的时候 makes the clause 'when I walked into the room', and 正在 shows his sleep was already under way.

examples.en: As soon as I walked into the restaurant, I got hungry.
examples.analysis: 一…就 'as soon as … then': 一 goes before the first verb, 走进饭馆, and 就 before the result. 饿了 with 了 marks a change of state: 'became hungry'.

examples.en: She walked into the classroom with a smile.
examples.analysis: 了 goes right after 走进 and before the place: 走进了教室 'walked into the classroom'. 笑着 'smiling' (verb + 着 before the main verb) says how she came in.

collocations.en: to walk in (away from the speaker)

senses.en: fluent, of speaking a language: 说得很流利
before a noun with 的: 流利的英语 'fluent English'

examples.en: You speak Chinese really fluently!
examples.analysis: Verb + 得 + adjective says how well something is done: 说得很流利 'speaks it fluently'. 很 gives a light 'very'; a bare 说得流利 tends to sound like a contrast with something else. A common compliment to learners.

examples.en: Does he speak English fluently?
examples.analysis: In a question, 流利 can follow 得 on its own: 说得流利吗 'does he speak it fluently?'. 英语 comes before the verb as the topic, the usual order when a 得 comment follows.

examples.zh: 我的普通话还不太流利。
examples.en: My Mandarin still isn't very fluent.
examples.analysis: 流利 works as a plain adjective predicate, with no 是: 普通话 + 不太流利 'not very fluent'. 还 'still' suggests the speaker expects to get there with time.

meaning: to ask the way; to ask for directions

senses.en: to ask (someone) for directions; it can split: 问了两次路

examples.en: I don't know the way, so I'll have to ask for directions.
examples.analysis: 问路 is a verb-object word, literally 'ask + road'. Here it follows 得 (děi) 'have to'. 不认识路 'don't know the way' is the everyday way to give the reason.

examples.en: Did he just come over to ask for directions?
examples.analysis: 来 + 问路 'came to ask the way': the second verb gives the purpose of coming. 是…的 puts the focus on that purpose, and 吗 asks yes or no.

examples.zh: 我问了两次路，还是没找到。
examples.en: I asked for directions twice and still couldn't find it.
examples.analysis: 问路 splits: 了 and the count 两次 'twice' go between 问 and 路. 还是 here means 'still': even after asking, 没找到 'didn't find (the place)'.

collocations.en: to find someone to ask the way

meaning: unpleasant to hear; (of words) rude, nasty

senses.en: unpleasant to listen to (a song, a voice, a noise); opposite of 好听
of words: rude, hurtful, offensive (说话很难听)

examples.en: His singing is awful.
examples.analysis: 难听 rates a sound: 唱歌 'singing' is the topic and 真难听 'really unpleasant to listen to' the comment. 真 'really' strengthens the judgment. The opposite is 好听.

examples.en: Don't say such nasty things.
examples.analysis: About words, 难听 means rude or hurtful, not just unpleasant to hear. 这么 + adjective + 的 + noun: 这么难听的话 'such nasty words'. 别 turns it into 'don't'.

examples.en: It doesn't sound bad! I actually like it.
examples.analysis: 不难听 'doesn't sound bad' is a mild defense, weaker than calling it 好听. 啊 adds a tone of gentle protest. 挺 means 'pretty, fairly' (挺喜欢的 'like it pretty well'), and the final 的 is optional.

senses.en: dictionary of words, on paper, in an app or online

examples.zh: 这个词我不认识，我查查词典。
examples.en: I don't know this word. Let me look it up in the dictionary.
examples.analysis: The verb for using a dictionary is 查 'look up': 查词典. Doubling it as 查查 makes it a quick, casual check. 这个词 comes first as the topic, then the comment 我不认识 'I don't recognize it'.

examples.zh: 你的词典能借我用用吗？
examples.en: Could I borrow your dictionary for a minute?
examples.analysis: 你的词典 is the topic at the front: 'your dictionary, can (you) lend (it to) me?'. 借我 'lend me' + 用用 'use it for a bit': the doubled verb makes the request sound small and casual.

examples.zh: 我不用词典，手机上就能查。
examples.en: I don't use a dictionary. I can just look things up on my phone.
examples.analysis: Here 用 is the verb 'use', so 不用词典 means 'don't use a dictionary', not 'no need'. 手机上 'on the phone' comes before the verb, and 就能查 'can simply look it up' stresses how easy that is.

collocations.en: to look something up in a dictionary

meaning: a tiny bit; just a little

senses.en: a tiny amount, before a noun: 一点点水 'a little water'
after an adjective: a tiny bit more (好一点点 'a little better')

examples.en: I can only speak a tiny bit of Chinese.
examples.analysis: 一点点 + noun: 'a tiny bit of Chinese'. It sounds smaller and more modest than 一点儿. With 只 'only' before 会, this is a very common modest thing to say about your Chinese.

examples.zh: 给我一点点就够了，谢谢。
examples.en: Just a little for me, that's enough. Thanks.
examples.analysis: Here 一点点 stands alone as the object of 给 'give': 'a little'. 就够了 'is enough': 就 stresses that this small amount is all that's needed. A polite line when someone is serving you food or drink.

examples.en: Today is a tiny bit better than yesterday.
examples.analysis: In a 比 comparison, 一点点 after the adjective tells how big the gap is: 比昨天好一点点 'a tiny bit better than yesterday'. It goes after 好, not before it.

related.en: a bit, before an adjective, often for complaints

senses.en: instant noodles, in a pack or a cup

measure.note: 一包方便面 'a pack of instant noodles'

examples.en: It's so late. Let's just have some instant noodles.
examples.analysis: 包 'pack' is the measure word for 方便面. Spoken Chinese often drops 一 before a measure word after a verb: 吃(一)包方便面. 吧 makes it a low-key suggestion.

examples.zh: 你又吃方便面？这样不健康。
examples.en: Instant noodles again? That's not healthy.
examples.analysis: 又 'again' marks something that keeps happening, often with a note of disapproval. The question has no 吗: the rising tone of voice shows surprise. 这样不健康 comments on the habit: 'this isn't healthy'.

examples.en: Do we still have any instant noodles at home?
examples.analysis: 家里还有…吗 'is there still any … at home?' checks what's left. 还 'still' + 有 'there is'. 方便面 takes no measure word here because only whether there are any matters, not how many.

collocations.en: to make instant noodles (soak in hot water)

senses.en: standard spoken Mandarin, the official spoken language of mainland China

examples.zh: 在北京，大家都说普通话吗？
examples.en: Does everyone in Beijing speak Mandarin?
examples.analysis: 说普通话 'speak Mandarin': with a language, the usual verb is 说 (讲 also works: 讲普通话). 大家都 'everyone, all' sits before the verb. 在北京 at the front sets the place for the whole question.

examples.zh: 他说的普通话我听不太懂。
examples.en: I can't really understand his Mandarin.
examples.analysis: 他说的普通话 'the Mandarin he speaks' is the topic, placed first. 听懂 'listen and understand' takes 不太 in the middle: 听不太懂 'can't quite understand (what I hear)'.

examples.en: Could you speak Mandarin, please?
examples.analysis: A polite request: 您 'you (polite)' + 能…吗 'can you …?'. You might say it to someone speaking a local dialect. 普通话 is the standard form taught in schools and used on national TV.

related.en: Chinese (the language as a whole, dialects included)
Chinese (the language), spoken or written; very common in everyday talk (说中文)

hook: 普通 'common, ordinary' + 话 'speech': the common speech.

senses.en: kilogram, the official unit; in daily talk 公斤 (kg) and 斤 (500 g) are more common

examples.zh: 飞机上只能带二十千克吗？
examples.en: Can you only take twenty kilos on the plane?
examples.analysis: Number + 千克, with no 个: 二十千克 'twenty kilograms'. 千克 is the official unit, the one on labels and forms; in conversation many people say 公斤. 只能 'can only' sets the limit.

examples.en: One kilogram is two jin.
examples.analysis: A handy conversion: a 斤 is half a kilo, so 一千克 = 两斤. Markets in China often price fruit and vegetables per 斤. 两 is the usual form before a measure word, though 二斤 is also heard.

examples.en: It's under a kilo, so you don't need to pay extra.
examples.analysis: 没有 + an amount means 'not reaching that amount': 没有一千克 'less than a kilogram'. 不用 'no need to' + 加钱 'add money'. A typical line at a courier counter.

meaning: afternoon nap; to nap after lunch

senses.en: to take a nap after lunch (我想午睡)
an after-lunch nap (午睡的习惯)

examples.en: Are you in the habit of napping after lunch?
examples.analysis: Here 午睡 + 的 describes 习惯, so it works like a noun: 午睡的习惯 'the habit of an after-lunch nap'. 有…的习惯 'have the habit of …' is a common frame. Many workplaces and schools in China leave time for a short nap after lunch.

examples.en: Once I've had lunch, I just want to nap.
examples.analysis: Verb use: 想午睡 'want to nap'. In 吃了午饭 + 就, 了 marks the first action as finished, and 就 shows the second follows right after it.

examples.zh: 小声一点儿，孩子在午睡。
examples.en: Keep it down a bit. The kids are napping.
examples.analysis: 在 + verb marks an action in progress: 在午睡 'is having a nap right now'. 小声一点儿 'a little quieter' is the request, and the second clause gives the reason.

collocations.en: to take an after-lunch nap (very common in speech)

meaning: to listen to a lecture or talk; to pay attention in class

senses.en: to listen to a teacher or speaker, in class or at a talk

examples.zh: 上课的时候要认真听讲。
examples.en: You need to pay attention in class.
examples.analysis: 认真听讲 'listen carefully to the teacher' is a set phrase from school. 听讲 means following someone who is teaching or giving a talk, not just hearing. 要 'need to' makes it advice; no subject is needed.

examples.zh: 他上课不听讲，老是看手机。
examples.en: He doesn't listen in class. He's always looking at his phone.
examples.analysis: 不听讲 'doesn't pay attention': 不 describes a habit, not a single event. 老是 'always' + 看手机 'looking at his phone' complains about something he does again and again.

examples.en: A lot of people came to the talk today.
examples.analysis: Here 听讲 means attending a talk or lecture, not just listening in class. In everyday speech people more often say 听讲座 for a public event; 听讲 alone sounds a little formal. In 来听讲的人 'the people who came to listen', the verb phrase + 的 describes 人. 很多 'many' is the comment, with no 是.

collocations.en: people who came to the talk

senses.en: the year before last (a time word, like 去年 'last year')

examples.en: I went to Beijing the year before last.
examples.analysis: 前年 is a time word: here it sits after the subject and before the verb, as 去年 would; it can also open the sentence (前年我去过北京). 去过 'have been to' marks the trip as a past experience.

examples.en: Did you guys meet the year before last?
examples.analysis: 是…的 focuses on when a past event happened, and 前年 is the time in focus. 认识 here means 'get to know each other', so the question asks when they first became acquainted.

examples.en: It wasn't this hot the year before last.
examples.analysis: 前年 can open the sentence as the topic. 没有 + 这么 + adjective, 'not as … as this', compares that year with now.

collocations.en: the summer of the year before last
the winter of the year before last

meaning: to celebrate the (Lunar) New Year; to spend New Year

senses.en: to celebrate Chinese (Lunar) New Year, the Spring Festival
to spend the New Year holiday somewhere (在北京过年); it can split: 过了年

examples.en: Are you going home for New Year this year?
examples.analysis: 回家过年 'go home for New Year': two verb phrases in a row, the second giving the purpose of the first. Hundreds of millions travel home for the holiday, so this is a standard question in winter.

examples.zh: 过了年我就去北京工作。
examples.en: After New Year, I'm going to Beijing to work.
examples.analysis: 过年 can split around 了: 过了年 'once New Year is over'. Followed by 就, it sets the time for the next step. 去北京工作 'go to Beijing to work' is another verb-plus-purpose pair.

examples.zh: 今年我们不回去了，在北京过年。
examples.en: We're not going back this year. We'll spend New Year in Beijing.
examples.analysis: 在 + place + 过年 'spend New Year in (a place)'. 不回去了 'not going back (this time)': the final 了 marks a change from the usual plan.

collocations.en: to go home for New Year
to have a good New Year

meaning: to take out; to produce (money, time, an idea)

senses.en: to take something out (of a bag, pocket, drawer): 拿出手机
to come up with, provide (money, time, a plan): 拿出时间

examples.en: He took a book out of his bag.
examples.analysis: 从 + place + 里 + 拿出 + thing: 'take (a thing) out of (a place)'. 拿 is the hand action and 出 the direction 'out'. The thing taken out comes after 拿出.

examples.en: Please take out your passport.
examples.analysis: A polite instruction you might hear at a counter or from a tour guide. 请 + verb means 'please …', and 拿出 takes its object directly: 拿出您的护照. Staff use 您, the polite 'you'.

examples.en: I can't come up with that much money.
examples.analysis: 不 between the two parts, 拿不出, means 'unable to take out', here 'can't come up with'. This is the 'provide, produce' sense: 拿出 money, time or a plan. 这么多钱 'this much money'.

senses.en: an evening newspaper
in a paper's name: 《北京晚报》 'Beijing Evening News'

measure.note: 一份晚报 'a copy of the evening paper'

examples.zh: 我爷爷很喜欢看《北京晚报》。
examples.en: My grandpa loves reading the Beijing Evening News.
examples.analysis: 晚报 is often part of a paper's name: 《北京晚报》. The everyday verb for reading a newspaper is 看. 很喜欢 'really likes': 很 adds real degree here, so 'loves' is the natural English.

examples.en: Has today's evening paper come yet?
examples.analysis: 今天的晚报 'today's evening paper': 的 links the time word to the noun. 来了吗 'has it arrived?': 了 marks the arrival as a new event, and 吗 asks whether it has happened.

examples.zh: 现在看晚报的人不多了。
examples.en: Not many people read the evening paper these days.
examples.analysis: 看晚报的人 'people who read the evening paper': a verb phrase + 的 describes 人. 不多了 'not many anymore': the final 了 shows the situation has changed from before.

collocations.en: a copy of the evening paper

meaning: to work; to do a job or chores (colloquial)

senses.en: to work, do a job: hands-on work, chores, or your job in general (colloquial)

examples.en: Stop messing around and come do some work!
examples.analysis: 干活儿 is the everyday word for doing work, especially hands-on jobs and chores. 快来 + verb 'come and … quickly'. 别…了 'stop …' tells someone to quit what they're doing.

examples.en: He's very conscientious about his work.
examples.analysis: Subject + activity + adjective: 他 + 干活儿 + 很认真 'he works conscientiously'. The activity sits before the description as a topic, so no 得 is needed.

examples.zh: 今天太累了，不想干活儿了。
examples.en: I'm so tired today. I don't feel like working anymore.
examples.analysis: 不想 + verb 'don't feel like …'. The final 了 marks a change: the speaker no longer wants to go on working. 太累了 'so tired' gives the reason.

related.en: to work for an employer, esp. a casual, part-time or manual job
